answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing tasks that counterparties verify and by staking tokens that are forfeited when a challenge proves fraud. A new identity starts with little stake and no trusted history, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply voting power; each account must fund its own stake and build a verified thread of work. The velvet rule is that rewards vest slowly, while a sable-weighted audit samples claims and slashes dishonest ones, making fake identities costly to create and risky to maintain.
